subject: Interop stress tests & availability asks — next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@cloudmed.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Interop stress tests & availability asks — next steps

Samantha / CloudMed team — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope the comparative reliability work you asked about (Redwood vs their hyperscaler endpoints):

Summary of priorities (from call)
- Primary: 99.95% production availability and predictable tail latency under spiky traffic.
- Secondary: graceful failover between regions and fallback to a lower-cost model when capacity is constrained.
- Constraints: cannot use customer PII in baseline stress tests; use synthetic payloads that mimic your real prompt mixes.

What Redwood proposes next (actionable items)
1) Joint stress window: 2-hour controlled run (canary -> full ramp -> soak) to exercise throughput, error rates, and failover. Proposed windows: Tue 2027-10-12 09:00–11:00 PT or Wed 2027-10-13 18:00–20:00 PT (pick one).
2) Test matrix: we attached an initial CSV with variants: seq_len distribution, concurrency steps, KV-cache warm vs cold, and simulated region outage toggles. Please confirm any additional scenarios.
3) Rate-limit and throttling probes: we will run gradual concurrency ramps and then small sustained spikes to measure rate limit behaviors and error budgets. We want to capture 99/99.9/99.99 latency percentiles and per-token error codes.
4) Failover validation: simulate primary-region packet loss and confirm fallback (model variant routing) within the agreed SLO window. We will instrument request traces and provide per-request routing metadata.
5) Deliverables: CSV with raw metrics, Grafana slices, and a short summary doc with recommended configuration (batching, quantization profiles) for your workload.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-test-matrix.csv (test cases), load-scripts.zip (synthetic runner), screenshot-error-budget-graph.png (example).

Please confirm the joint window that works for your ops team and any additional success criteria to add to the matrix. Once we have a time, Jordan will share runbooks and a temporary test API key.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
redwood.com

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Traffic profile: our production 90th percentile request size is ~480 tokens; 95th ~1,200 tokens. Peak QPS per region today is ~450 requests/sec during business hours; we can run a reduced-scale test at 200–300 qps for safety.
2) Success criteria: we need failed requests to be <0.02% during the steady period, and failover to complete within 25s for >95% of requests when simulating a regional interruption.
3) Security: we prefer tests run over a private peering connection if possible; otherwise use TLS-only endpoints and scrubbed payloads.
4) Timing: Tue 2027-10-12 09:00–11:00 PT works for us — please confirm run-book and lead contacts.

I'll loop in our lead DevOps contact (it@cloudmed.com) for scheduling and to share an internal runbook. We may also want to validate how the hyperscaler handles 429 vs 503 under the same spike profile.

—Sam
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Platform Engineering, CloudMed
samantha.ortiz@cloudmed.com

Subject: Re: Interop stress tests & availability asks — next steps

Great — Tue 10/12 09:00–11:00 PT is locked. A few follow-ups and owners so we have a tight plan: 

Run owners
- Redwood lead: Jordan Blake (jordan.blake@redwood.com) — instrumentation, temporary keys, Grafana slices.
- Redwood infra: Stephanie Nguyen (stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com) — orchestrates load injection and region failover toggles.
- CloudMed lead: Samantha Ortiz / DevOps team — traffic shaping, private peering confirmation.

Concrete test checklist (we will produce a short runbook)
- Canary: 15m at 50% expected final qps (warm caches). Capture p50/p90/p99 latency, error rates, and token throughput.
- Ramp: linear ramp to target qps (200–300) over 20m, hold 30m for steady window.
- Spike: three 60s sudden spikes to 2x target qps to probe throttling and 429/503 behavior.
- Failover: during steady hold, initiate a region blackhole test and observe routing fallback time and error transition states.
- Post-run: 30m soak with reduced concurrency to validate recovery and warm-cache behavior.

Data capture and labels
- Each request will include: test-id, region, model-variant, batch-size, and request-token-count. Please confirm CloudMed can capture request metadata at their side for cross-correlation.

Success criteria we’ll verify in the summary
- Failed requests under steady window <0.02%
- Failover completion for >95% of requests within 25s (aligns with your ask)
- 99.9th latency < 2.5x our p50 baseline during steady window (measure will be shown in Grafana)

We will share the runbook + temporary keys by Fri 2027-10-08 COB. Jordan — can you attach the preliminary Grafana dashboards and the test harness repo here when ready? Stephanie — please confirm if we need a peering IP range for the private run or if TLS-only is the fallback.

Ben
